about: Hand-kept wiki data that the specs do not carry. generate_wiki.py merges it into the generated wiki database (web/wiki-app/public/db/). Edit this file, never the generated JSON. epics: a name, phase and engine per epic folder (an epic not listed takes its name from its README and phase 5). overlays: per generated entry id, a hand-written summary (put before the spec text), extra tags, related ids, endpoints and tables and metadata. entries: whole entries with no spec of their own (the implementation phases, wiki pages, tables named only in a review). cross_refs: the file inventory and build order published in wiki-cross-refs.json.

diagram-auth-flow.summary: Web cookie login + native JWT login + refresh rotation + logout + device pairing.

diagram-client-stories.summary: Story-relationship map for Epics 11-17 (Web UI, Mobile, Desktop, TV, Discovery, Subscriptions, Design system).

diagram-data-flow.summary: End-to-end data flow from new file landed on disk → scan → probe → transcribe → index → categorize → browse → play.

diagram-epic-dependencies.summary: Epic-level dependency edges across all 24 epics. Identifies the first-to-land epic.

diagram-job-lifecycle.summary: Queue worker state machine: pending → running → succeeded / failed / paused / cancelled / retrying.

diagram-search-architecture.summary: Indexer + FTS + semantic embeddings + hybrid scorer feeding /search.

diagram-security-architecture.summary: Trust boundaries, JWKS publication, signed-URL minter, Streaming offline JWT verify, CSRF, secret loading, transport hardening.

diagram-streaming-flow.summary: Session create → pinned transcoder → manifest → segment → close. Includes hwaccel branch and direct/remux/transcode mode-pick.

diagram-system-architecture.summary: Macro topology — Pipeline (Python), API (Go), Streaming (Go), Postgres, media volume, web/mobile/desktop/TV clients, mDNS, and the gRPC + REST + WS edges.

entity-audio_tracks.summary: One row per audio stream — index, codec, channels, sample rate, language (ISO 639-3), title, is_default, disposition, detected_language.

entity-audit_log.summary: Canonical append-only audit table partitioned by month. category column distinguishes 'library' (story 9.17) from 'security' (story 10.16). Triggers reject UPDATE / DELETE.

entity-chapters.summary: Inferred chapter boundaries with start/end seconds and language tag. Drives HLS DATERANGE + chapter sidebar.

entity-devices.summary: Per-device push tokens (ios / android / web). UNIQUE (user_id, platform, push_token).

entity-libraries.summary: One row per user-defined library. Holds roots, settings (disabled, follow_symlinks, language), and timestamps.

entity-library_scan_state.summary: Per-library scan progress: sweep IDs, visited / inserted / updated / skipped / marked-missing counters, timestamps.

entity-media_features.summary: Per-video probe-derived signals (music/speech ratio, silence%, LUFS, density).

entity-media_info.summary: Per-video container, video codec, resolution, fps, bitrate, has_subtitles, raw ffprobe JSONB. Probe cache.

entity-processing_jobs.summary: Single durable queue table for every pipeline stage. Fields include id, video_id, stage, state, priority, not_before, claimed_by, claimed_at, attempts, max_attempts, last_heartbeat_at, last_segment_end_sec (canonical resume), pause_requested, cancel_requested, error JSON. Indexed for claim, lookup, reaper, flag-poll.

entity-search_suggestion_terms.summary: Pre-computed 2-/3-/4-grams per library with frequencies. Backs autocomplete.

entity-stt_usage.summary: OpenAI-API ledger: per-library monthly USD spend, enforces max_usd_per_month cap before claim.

entity-subtitle_files.summary: One row per discovered or generated subtitle file. format (srt/vtt), language, path, is_external, is_embedded.

entity-track_selection_decisions.summary: Audit trail of selected track(s), decision rule, rejected tracks with rationale.

entity-transcript_segments.summary: Per-segment STT output: text, confidence, start_sec, end_sec, optional speaker, optional word-level data. Sequence enforced monotonically.

entity-transcript_units.summary: Search units chunked from segments (~200 char target / 400 hard cap). Single source of truth for FTS and vector indexes. Has GENERATED tsvector column.

entity-transcript_words.summary: Optional word-level timestamps and confidences (when the backend supplies them).

entity-transcripts.summary: One row per transcription pass. is_active partial-UNIQUE marks the live one; history rows kept for reprocessing. Tracks backend, model, parameters, progress.

entity-users.summary: argon2id password hashes; is_admin flag; failed_attempts + locked_until. Sentinel UUID 00000000-...-001 for single-user mode.

entity-vector_index_dead_letter.summary: Retry queue for failed Chroma writes during the post-transcribe index stage.

entity-videos.summary: One row per discovered file. Carries content_hash, path, filename, size_bytes, mtime, state (FSM owned by Story 1.6). UNIQUE (library_id, content_hash).

epic-01-scanner.summary: Detect every video file under a library's roots, assign a stable identity (content_hash via BLAKE3 head+tail+size), and create videos rows in DISCOVERED state. Cope with renames, moves, copies, partial downloads, lying network filesystems, and 200 GB drag-and-drops.

epic-02-audio-extraction.summary: Probe a video, pick the right audio track, extract mono 16 kHz s16le PCM, and feed it into the transcriber without an intermediate WAV when the backend can consume a stream. Record the chosen track in audio_tracks.

epic-03-transcription.summary: Convert extracted audio into transcript_segments with second-accurate timestamps. Multiple swappable STT backends (mlx-whisper, faster-whisper, openai). Per-segment durable commits, exact pause/resume, bidi-correct Arabic. The long-running stage and primary consumer of the job queue.

epic-04-subtitles.summary: Generate well-formed SRT and VTT sidecars from finalized transcripts. Auto-discover external subtitle files. Lazily extract embedded subtitle tracks from MKVs. Streaming Service can render live VTT directly from transcript_segments.

epic-05-search-indexing.summary: Make every transcribed second searchable in two complementary ways — exact-phrase / proximity (Postgres tsvector or SQLite FTS5) and semantic (ChromaDB) — and fuse them into one ranked result set with language filters, deep-linkable timestamps, and Arabic-correct snippet highlighting.

metadata.owner: Pipeline writes both indexes; API service reads (proxies semantic queries via gRPC Embed)

epic-06-job-queue.summary: Durable, atomic, pause-aware job queue. Single Postgres table (processing_jobs); no broker, no Celery, no Redis. All claim, heartbeat, retry, pause, resume, cancel, and reaper logic lives here. Every other pipeline epic depends on this.

epic-07-api-server.summary: Go API Service. Every request that isn't a media byte: library CRUD, search, job control, settings, watch state, real-time WebSocket fan-out, gRPC client surface to Pipeline and Streaming. Stateless behind Postgres; one binary scales horizontally without session affinity.

epic-08-streaming.summary: Go Streaming Service. Every media byte: HLS / DASH manifests, range-served direct play, FFmpeg-driven transcode and remux, live subtitle muxing, sprite/poster serving, session-pinned adaptive playback. Validates JWTs offline against the API's published JWKS so a playing video survives an API restart.

epic-09-library-management.summary: Long-lived behaviors that turn a folder on disk into a curated, browsable catalog: filesystem watching, dedup, auto-categorization, organization primitives (collections, smart collections, tags, speakers), library lifecycle, chapter inference.

epic-10-auth-security.summary: Identity, sessions, signed URLs, secret handling, transport hardening. Two surfaces, one identity: web cookies + CSRF and native bearer JWT + refresh. Streaming verifies JWTs offline against the API's published JWKS. First epic to land — Epic 7 endpoints depend on this epic's primitives.

epic-11-web-ui.summary: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite SPA. PWA-installable, RTL-first, WCAG 2.1 AA, offline-capable for everything except video bytes. Source bundle for Capacitor (mobile) and Tauri (desktop).

epic-12-mobile.summary: iOS and Android apps wrapping the web bundle. Native player handoff, background download, push notifications, share targets, Keychain/Keystore for refresh tokens.

epic-13-desktop.summary: Tauri 2 wrapper of the web bundle. Native binaries for macOS / Windows / Linux. Tray, mDNS discovery, drag-drop, auto-update.

epic-14-tv-apps.summary: Native tvOS (Swift / SwiftUI / AVPlayer) and Android TV (Kotlin / Compose for TV / ExoPlayer) apps consuming the same GraphQL schema as every other client. 10-foot UI, D-pad navigation, voice search, HDR pass-through, Continue Watching + Recommendations rows.

epic-15-discovery.summary: mDNS LAN discovery, opt-in cloud relay (QUIC + SPKI pinning), server-to-server federation (X25519 + Ed25519 + SAS), UPnP/DLNA compatibility, QR pairing. All cross-instance features ship off and require explicit user action.

epic-16-subscriptions.summary: Optional premium tier (home / pro) gated by Ed25519-signed license key; free tier remains fully functional. the payment provider's (TBD) customer portal for billing; opt-in telemetry; per-tier feature flags with cohorts.

epic-17-ux-design-system.summary: Design tokens as single source of truth; Style Dictionary build pipeline emits CSS / Swift / Kotlin / JSON; React + Storybook component library with Chromatic visual regression; RTL-first (Arabic baseline); respect OS preferences (dark mode, reduced motion, high contrast).

epic-18-performance.summary: Per-endpoint p50/p95/p99 budgets in shared/perf_budgets.yaml; warm/cold cache tags; single-flight on cold paths; embed deadline 200ms with FTS-only fallback; cache hit-rate floors; soak test detecting <1 MiB/h leak.

epic-19-scalability.summary: Single-host capacity floor (50k videos / 1M segments / 30 TB on Mac mini M2); stateless API with NOTIFY+events fan-out; sticky-session streaming; SKIP LOCKED pipeline coordination; Postgres replica with lag-aware routing; bounded-memory cold scan; concurrency caps; multi-tenant readiness via flag flip.

epic-20-testing.summary: Three-tier pyramid (unit / integration / e2e) with Go build tags / pytest marks / TS suffixes; per-tier runtime budgets (60s / 8m / 12m); fixture corpus; coverage floors; contract drift fails CI; perf regression CI; flake auto-quarantine.

epic-21-observability.summary: Structured JSON logs with required base fields; per-service /metrics with strict cardinality (no per-row labels); OTel distributed tracing with W3C traceparent + composite head sampler; /healthz + /readyz + /api/system/health; UUIDv7 error_id with rate-limited webhook; append-only partitioned audit_log; queue/job visibility; default-off outbound telemetry with redaction.

epic-22-devops.summary: Six-gate CI (lint/unit/integration/e2e/perf-ci/build-artifacts); reproducible builds via -trimpath, uv lock, pnpm lock, ko, cosign, minisign; four multi-arch container images + Caddy reverse proxy; Goose migrations with linter; SemVer tagging + CHANGELOG gate; doctor pre-flight + drain-mode rolling restart + version-jump guard; multi-platform packaging (Homebrew, deb/rpm, Capacitor mobile, Tauri desktop, native TV).

epic-23-security.summary: Argon2id password hashing + RS256 JWT (15 min access, 30d refresh) + JWKS rotation (90d / 30d overlap); ACL via library_acl with JWT lib claim canonical for streaming; Caddy TLS 1.2+ + HSTS + inter-service mTLS via in-process CA; secrets precedence _FILE > env > config + log redaction; input validation including paths.canonical_under_roots; rate limits + failed-login lockout; SBOM + CVE scan gate; coordinated disclosure.

epic-24-data-integrity.summary: Atomic sidecar writes (temp + fsync + atomic rename); idempotent + resumable jobs with key (content_hash, stage, backend, model, config_hash); FK/unique/CHECK constraints + soft-delete partial unique; SKIP LOCKED + advisory locks + ChromaDB single-writer; daily pg_dump backups with verify; four DR scenarios with RTO/RPO; weekly integrity doctor; identity stability via BLAKE3 sample hash + superseded_by; forward-back compat via schema_version + cache key major prefix.

epic-25-cloud-relay.summary: Maktaba Cloud — hosted SaaS layer (HamzaLabs): identity, server linking, WSS-tunneled HTTP relay, push fanout, provider-neutral billing (payment provider TBD), plus native installers for macOS / Windows / Linux / NAS / ARM / VPS.

review-full_implementation_audit.summary: End-to-end audit of `main` (post-merge of #12) against the 272 story acceptance criteria. Surfaced 5 blockers, 8 majors, 11 minors; tracks which were resolved in the audit-blockers cleanup PR (#19).

story-10.1.summary: users table with argon2id password hashes. Sentinel UUID 00000000-...-001 reserved for single-user mode.

story-10.10.summary: Double-submit cookie pattern: csrf_token cookie + matching X-CSRF-Token header on every state-changing web request.

story-10.11.summary: Per-account failed-attempts counter + locked_until. Backoff increases on repeated failures.

story-10.12.summary: Per-IP and per-user token-bucket on /auth/* — separate from generic API rate limiting (7.19).

story-10.13.summary: Admin / viewer split for v1. Permission middleware checks is_admin and resource ownership.

story-10.14.summary: Secrets loaded from env / file / KMS. log redaction filter strips known-secret patterns.

story-10.15.summary: TLS termination, HSTS, secure cookies, restrictive CORS allowlist. Mandatory in production.

story-10.16.summary: Writes category='security' rows to the canonical audit_log table owned by epic 9.

story-10.17.summary: 8-char base32 pairing code displayed on signed-in device, claimed by new device.

story-10.2.summary: httpOnly auth cookie + readable csrf_token cookie. CSRF middleware (10.10) checks header on every state-changing request.

story-10.3.summary: RS256 JWT access (short TTL) + opaque refresh (argon2id-hashed at rest, family-bound).

story-10.4.summary: Refresh rotation: every refresh issues a new opaque token. Reuse of a revoked refresh token revokes the entire family.

story-10.5.summary: Web: revoke web_session row. Native: revoke entire refresh family.

story-10.6.summary: RS256 keypair lifecycle. JWKS endpoint published for offline verifiers.

story-10.7.summary: Streaming caches JWKS and verifies session JWTs without calling the API. Library-scoped lib[] claim enforces per-segment authorization.

story-10.8.summary: Single minter consumed by API to produce streaming URLs. Auds: streaming, streaming-direct, streaming-static, api.

story-10.9.summary: Opt-in single-user/admin token bypass. Audit attribution uses sentinel UUID.

story-11.1.summary: Library list with grid + list views, sort and filter rail. Targets paginated reads via 7.4.

story-11.10.summary: Workbox service worker. Caches shell, metadata, posters. Video bytes never cached at this layer.

story-11.11.summary: axe-core in CI; reduced-motion; every interactive control reachable by keyboard.

story-11.12.summary: i18n table is the only string source; no literal strings in JSX. RTL is first-class.

story-11.13.summary: User-issued PATs for CLI / extension integrations. argon2id-hashed at rest with scopes.

story-11.14.summary: Reads from web_sessions and refresh_tokens; surfaces a unified session list with revoke.

story-11.2.summary: Hero, metadata, transcript jumps, related items.

story-11.3.summary: Vidstack-based HLS player. Captions, chapters, sprite scrubber. Player join time targets.

story-11.4.summary: FTS / semantic / hybrid toggle, facets, transcript hit list. p50 ≤ 250 ms.

story-11.5.summary: Per-stage counts, retry/cancel, real-time updates via WebSocket.

story-11.6.summary: Libraries, STT backend selection, players, theme, language.

story-11.7.summary: Breakpoints: phone, tablet, desktop, large desktop. Token-driven.

story-11.8.summary: User-toggle + system-pref default. Tokens shipped from epic 17.

story-11.9.summary: Global and per-page shortcut tables. Discoverable via ? overlay.

story-12.1.summary: Capacitor 6 iOS shell over the web bundle.

story-12.10.summary: Owns the contract behind /devices/* (handlers in epic 7 / 7.22). Server-side push fan-out.

story-12.11.summary: Per-device downloaded state on watch progress; reconciles when device comes online.

story-12.2.summary: Capacitor 6 Android shell over the web bundle.

story-12.3.summary: AVPlayer (iOS) / ExoPlayer (Android) consumes HLS via 8.5. Bypasses Vidstack on mobile for background playback / AirPlay / Chromecast / lock-screen controls.

story-12.4.summary: APNs (iOS) and FCM (Android). Server fan-out reads from devices table.

story-12.5.summary: Audio continues when the app is backgrounded; lock-screen and CarPlay-equivalent controls.

story-12.6.summary: Native download manager. Progress, pause/resume, integrity check on completion.

story-12.8.summary: Capacitor Haptics plugin for select, success, warning patterns.

story-12.9.summary: Universal Links (iOS) + App Links (Android). Single-instance reuse.

story-13.4.summary: Tray icon menu listing active streams and queue. Platform-specific iconography.

story-13.5.summary: SD-DNS query for _maktaba._tcp; TOFU prompt before any credentials cross the wire.

story-13.6.summary: OS file drag-drop hands files to the standard ingest path.

story-13.8.summary: Tauri signed-update endpoint. Channels: stable / beta / canary.

story-14.1.summary: tvOS 17+ SwiftUI app with AVPlayer HLS+HDR playback, Top Shelf extension, Apollo iOS GraphQL client, QR pairing as issuer, Apple TV Remote support.

story-14.2.summary: Android TV 9+ Compose for TV app, ExoPlayer HLS+HDR, Recommendations Channel via WorkManager + PreviewChannel API, Apollo Kotlin client.

story-14.3.summary: TV-specific type scale (28-96pt), focus rings, D-pad geometry primitives, safe-area insets, FocusableCardStyle.

story-14.4.summary: Siri App Intents + SFSpeechRecognizer (tvOS); Google Assistant action + RecognizerIntent (Android TV); did-you-mean suggestions.

story-14.5.summary: Home screen first row populated from playback_state (5-95% watched), recency-sorted, cross-device sync via WS playback.changed events.

story-14.6.summary: Up to 5 rows x <=20 items with localized titles + reasons; Not interested dismissal; cached 24h server-side.

story-14.7.summary: Nightly batch recommender: semantic similarity over media_features embeddings + speaker heuristic (>=3 watches) + library affinity + cold-start; 60s in-process LRU cache.

story-7.1.summary: chi-based HTTP server, RFC 9457 problem+json error envelope, UUID v7 request IDs, structured logging via slog, graceful shutdown, idempotency-key replay store.

story-7.10.summary: Create / get / close streaming sessions; mints session JWTs via 10.8 and calls Streaming OpenSession via gRPC.

story-7.11.summary: Per-user, per-video watch position; debounced PUT, cursor read.

story-7.12.summary: Pause / resume / cancel / retry for individual queue jobs.

story-7.13.summary: Aggregate per-stage counts and bottleneck signals.

story-7.14.summary: CRUD for organization primitives whose behavior is in epic 9.

story-7.15.summary: Read/write app settings; STT backend probe; system meta.

story-7.16.summary: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY → WebSocket fan-out per user. No Redis or in-process bus.

story-7.17.summary: Single /graphql endpoint layered over the REST resolvers. Generated TS types in shared/graphql/schema.graphql.

story-7.18.summary: Code-generated gRPC clients; load-balanced and connection-pooled; integrates with story 7.10.

story-7.19.summary: Schema validation on all writes; body size caps; per-IP and per-user token-bucket rate limits.

story-7.2.summary: Shared cursor pagination across all list endpoints. Opaque base64 cursor, no offset.

story-7.20.summary: Liveness/readiness, build-version endpoint, Prometheus /metrics. OpenTelemetry traces.

story-7.21.summary: Per-user recommendations from semantic features and watch history.

story-7.22.summary: Register / list / revoke device push tokens. Required by mobile epic for push fan-out.

story-7.3.summary: GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE for /libraries. Multi-root and validation surfaces handled here; behavior in epic 9.

story-7.4.summary: List, retrieve, partial-update, and delete videos with cursor pagination and rich filters.

story-7.5.summary: Start, restart, pause, resume, cancel processing for a video.

story-7.6.summary: Window-paginated transcript segments around a target time.

story-7.7.summary: Read-only access to subtitle tracks and chapter lists for a video.

story-7.8.summary: Three search modes via one endpoint with mode toggle. Targets p50 ≤ 250 ms on 100k-segment fixture.

story-7.9.summary: Persisted user search queries; consumed by smart collections (9.14).

story-8.1.summary: Streaming service chassis. All paths validate JWTs offline against the JWKS published by 10.6.

story-8.10.summary: Per-host slot accounting; over-cap requests get 503 Retry-After, never connection drops.

story-8.11.summary: Mux subtitles into HLS at request time from auto-generated VTT, sidecar files, or embedded streams.

story-8.12.summary: Inline HLS DATERANGE tags and a sidecar JSON for non-HLS players.

story-8.13.summary: Static derivation artifacts served behind streaming-static JWT scope.

story-8.14.summary: On-disk cache for HLS segments and probe artifacts; LRU eviction; configurable cap.

story-8.15.summary: FFprobe results memoized in Postgres + LRU; eviction triggered by file-hash change.

story-8.2.summary: Maps client → supported codecs / containers / DRM tiers. Picks playback mode (direct / remux / transcode).

story-8.3.summary: Pass-through byte range serving when client supports the source format.

story-8.4.summary: Container-only remux when codecs are compatible but container isn't (e.g. MKV → MP4).

story-8.5.summary: Full FFmpeg transcode to multi-rendition HLS. Canonical adaptive format.

story-8.6.summary: DASH alternative to HLS, opt-in at session create.

story-8.7.summary: VAAPI / NVENC / VideoToolbox probing; auto-fallback to software encode on probe failure.

story-8.8.summary: Inter-service contract consumed by the API binary (story 7.10 / 7.18).

story-8.9.summary: Session store pins each session to a single Streaming host. Reaper closes idle sessions.

story-9.1.summary: JSON schema for library configuration. Multi-root rejection happens at write time.

story-9.10.summary: Music vs speech vs hybrid signal from probe metrics.

story-9.11.summary: Cluster diarized voices into speaker entities; rename, merge, split.

story-9.12.summary: User-defined and auto tags. Lowercase / collapse-whitespace normalization at write.

story-9.14.summary: A smart collection is a name + saved-search ID + ordering policy. Zero duplication of the search logic.

story-9.15.summary: Two modes: catalog-only (preserves files) and full purge (deletes both). Cascade through videos → streaming_sessions.

story-9.16.summary: Reject two libraries claiming overlapping roots; warn on near-overlap.

story-9.17.summary: Append-only audit rows for library mutations. Shares the canonical audit_log table with epic 10 (story 10.16) — distinguished by category column.

story-9.18.summary: Heuristic chapter boundaries from segment-embedding topic transitions.

story-9.2.summary: Python watchdog observer per library. Debounced; waits for size and mtime to settle before ingest.

story-9.3.summary: Cadence-driven catch-up sweep that fills gaps when the watcher misses events.

story-9.4.summary: Partial-content hash (head + tail + length) avoids full-file reads on large files.

story-9.5.summary: .gitignore-style ignore rules + extension allowlist applied before any pipeline work.

story-9.6.summary: API-triggered scan with progress events surfaced over WebSocket.

story-9.7.summary: < 50 ms target; trigger-maintained cache table backs the query.

story-9.8.summary: Per-video language detection from the transcribe stage output.

story-9.9.summary: K-means recluster of segment embeddings; centroids re-computed on cadence.

entries.title: Phase 3 — Pipeline foundations — Subtitles + Search
entries.content: Epics 4-5: subtitle generation, FTS via tsvector, Chroma vector backend, hybrid RRF, incremental indexing, query suggestions, chapter inference.

entries.title: Phase 4 — Job queue + Pipeline daemon wiring
entries.content: Epic 6 durable job queue with claim loop, heartbeat, pause/resume/cancel, backoff, reaper, concurrency caps, graceful shutdown.

entries.title: Phase 5 — Subtitles + Search indexing closeout
entries.content: Phase 5 closed out Epics 4-5 and validated the cross-epic search RRF + subtitle live-VTT contract integration.

entries.title: Phase 6 — API server (Epic 7)
entries.content: API CRUD/search/sessions/settings — HTTP skeleton, cursor pagination, library CRUD, ingest endpoints, GraphQL SDL, gRPC clients to Pipeline + Streaming.

entries.title: Phase 7 — Streaming service (Epic 8)
entries.content: HLS/DASH origin: signed-URL gating, capability matrix, direct play, remux, hwaccel, gRPC session lifecycle, subtitle/chapter/poster/sprite cache.

entries.title: Phase 8 — Library management (Epic 9)
entries.content: Library config schema, multi-root overlap detection, ignore rules, periodic sweep, content-hash dedup, manual scan controls, audit log.

entries.title: Phase 9 — Auth & security hardening (Epic 10)
entries.content: User store, web/native login, RS256 + JWKS, signed URLs, single-user mode, CSRF, brute-force + rate limiting, transport security, audit log.

entries.title: Phase 10 — Web UI (Epic 11)
entries.content: React 18 PWA: library browse, video detail, player with transcript, search results, settings, auth flows. Shared with Capacitor/Tauri wrappers.

entries.title: Phase 11 — Mobile + desktop shells (Epics 12-13)
entries.content: Capacitor wrappers (iOS/Android) with native plugins for background download, file association, push, native player handoff. Tauri 2 desktop wrapper.

entries.title: Phase 12 — TV apps + discovery (Epics 14-15)
entries.content: Native tvOS (Swift / AVPlayer) + Android TV (Kotlin / ExoPlayer). mDNS discovery, QR pairing, LAN-first connection flow.

entries.title: Phase 13 — Subscriptions + UX design system (Epics 16-17)
entries.content: Local subscriptions (sources, schedules, RSS, podcast), and the cross-platform design system (tokens, components, motion, RTL).

entries.title: Phase 14 — Performance + scalability (Epics 18-19)
entries.content: Performance budgets, caching, lazy hydration, scalability targets, single-box 30TB validation, worker concurrency tuning.

entries.title: Phase 15 — Testing + observability (Epics 20-21)
entries.content: Test pyramid with tier budgets and CI enforcement, OpenTelemetry traces + metrics, structured logs, error envelopes, health/readiness probes.

entries.title: Phase 16 — DevOps + security + data integrity (Epics 22-24)
entries.content: CI pipelines, container images, migrations infra, security hardening, supply chain, atomic writes, idempotent jobs, backup/restore, disaster recovery.

entries.title: Phase 17 — Cloud Relay (Epic 25)
entries.content: Maktaba Cloud SaaS layer: identity, server claim, WSS tunnel, HTTP relay proxy, bandwidth metering, provider-neutral billing, push fanout, admin consoles, installers, entitlement signing.

entries.title: app_settings
entries.content: Runtime-editable knobs as key/value JSONB. NOTIFY 'settings_changed' on UPDATE/INSERT.

entries.title: streaming_sessions
entries.content: One row per active session. Cascades through videos.library_id. Indexed for the idle-reaper and per-user lookup.

entries.title: library_topics + video_topics
entries.content: Per-library topic centroids (k-means recluster) and per-video topic membership scores.

entries.title: library_sweeps
entries.content: One row per sweep run; new/moved/removed counts and any error JSON.

entries.title: library_stats_cache
entries.content: Trigger-maintained cache backing the < 50 ms /libraries/{id}/stats target.

entries.title: web_sessions
entries.content: One row per cookie session with CSRF token, IP, UA, expiry. Reaper-indexed.

entries.title: refresh_tokens
entries.content: argon2id-hashed opaque refresh tokens. family_id shared across the rotation chain.

entries.title: pairing_codes
entries.content: 8-char base32 device-pairing codes. state = pending / claimed / expired.

entries.title: Security architecture summary
entries.content: Cross-cutting summary: auth flow (web cookie, native JWT pair, sentinel admin token, QR pairing), JWT lifecycle (RS256 mint/rotate/JWKS/verify with kid), signed URLs, rate limits + lockout, input validation, TLS + HSTS + mTLS + TOFU, secrets precedence + redaction, supply chain, ACL roles. Cross-references Epic 10 + Epic 23 + Epic 15 + Epic 21.

entries.title: Migration catalog

entries.title: Project glossary
entries.content: Project-specific terminology used across specs/, plans, mockups, and code. Curated from epic READMEs, plans, stories. Each entry includes definition + where used.

parallel_tracks: Pipeline (Epics 1–6) and API/Streaming (Epics 7, 8) — independent after Phase 1; gRPC contract is the shared interface.
Web (Epic 11), Mobile (Epic 12), Desktop (Epic 13) — all wrap the same web bundle; sequential or parallel.
TV (Epic 14) — shares no code with web; can be built in parallel by a separate person.
NFR epics (18–24) — accrete tests/infrastructure on top of feature work; run in parallel with feature epics.
Discovery (15), Subscriptions (16), Design system (17) — largely orthogonal to backend work.

reviews.scope: architecture.md + 4 epic documents (Pipeline, API/Streaming, Clients/Discovery, NFR)
reviews.summary: Cross-document audit. All 18 blockers and 24 majors raised in §8 are resolved. §7 build order is the canonical implementation sequence.

Migration-slot conflicts (7), naming-convention violations (3), code-blocker bugs (10), cross-plan ownership conflicts (3), schema deviations vs architecture §8.1 — all fixed. Migration slots now tracked centrally in shared/db/migrations/MANIFEST.md.

reviews.scope: Epics 07–13 (API, Streaming, Library, Auth, Web, Mobile, Desktop)
reviews.summary: Schema drift (Epics 07/08/09), ID type drift (BIGSERIAL vs UUID), table-name drift, FSM state casing, gRPC contract drift vs §9.9, subtitle_gen stage owner, devices-table double-ownership, audit_log category enum, refresh_tokens.device_id, device-pat auth source, Web UI calling endpoints not in Epic 07, Tauri 2 ACL capabilities, migration ordering. Architecture.md updated as canonical, then 105 plans swept.

Two double-ownership bugs (recommendations endpoint, pairing endpoint) where two plans defined the same route with incompatible schemas — now resolved. Three plans shippable as-is: 17-03 motion, 17-04 loading-states, 17-05 error-empty-states.

reviews.scope: Epics 18–24 (NFR: Performance, Scalability, Testing, Observability, DevOps, Security, Data Integrity)

Epic 23 ↔ Epic 10 contradictions resolved with explicit canonical ownership: Epic 23 wins on authz (three-role) + rate-limit numbers (with 10-12's library); Epic 10 wins on HSTS placement + JWT key storage. Architecture §3 (lowercase states), §9.9 (Streaming superset), new §11.6 (telemetry block) updated.
